title: DispatchHealthPanel is built and tested but mounted nowhere
body:
## Summary
The dispatch-health panel (sent/acked/in-flight/stuck/failed from the cli.* bus) has zero render sites; its only reference is the cli barrel index.ts, which itself has zero importers.

## Description
src/components/cli/DispatchHealthPanel.tsx:19 renders computeDispatchHealth (src/components/cli/dispatchHealth.ts:55) over cli.* events that src/lib/event-bus-bridge.ts:47-97 still emits. It was added as 'the permanent monitor the SP-A->SP-B remediation deserved', but no shell, dev page or module renders it, so the stuck-dispatch signal it computes is observed by nobody. Fixed = mounted on an operator-chosen diagnostics surface, or retired with its test.

## Flow
- git grep DispatchHealthPanel -> only src/components/cli/index.ts and the file itself
- git grep "from '@/components/cli'" -> 0 importers of the barrel
- so no UI path renders the panel

## Expected impact
Operators would see in-flight/stuck dispatch counts while a run hangs instead of after wall-clock runs out. Where it lives is a product call; nothing breaks either way.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - make the built dispatch-health monitor observable
Before: 0 render sites
After: 1 render site on a diagnostics surface (or 0 files if retired)
Method: probe - grep of render sites; the placement itself is a product choice no instrument decides
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/cli/DispatchHealthPanel.tsx:19
src/components/cli/index.ts:2
$ git grep -l DispatchHealthPanel -> context-map.json, src/components/cli/{DispatchHealthPanel.tsx,dispatchHealth.test.ts,dispatchHealth.ts,index.ts}
$ git grep -n "from '@/components/cli'" -> (none)
instrument: operator picks the host surface; then a render test asserting the panel appears there

title: Closing a running inline terminal orphans its server-side Claude process
body:
## Summary
InlineTerminal's Close (X) calls removeSession while the session may be running; CompactTerminal unmounts and only closes its EventSource, so the spawned CLI keeps editing files with no handle left to abort it.

## Description
src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:155 calls removeSession(sessionId) unconditionally. removeSession (src/components/cli/store/cliPanelStore.ts:215) deletes the session including currentExecutionId, the only persisted handle to the run. useTaskQueue's unmount cleanup closes the stream but never DELETEs /api/claude-terminal/query?executionId=. Per subprocess-lifecycle termination-and-reaping (creation names its reaper) the close path must abort the run first or confirm. Fixed = Close on a running session aborts the execution (DELETE) before removal, or asks via the shared ConfirmDialog.

## Flow
- user starts a run in an inline terminal
- clicks X (Close terminal) while 'running'
- session removed -> component unmounts -> EventSource closed
- server process keeps running until its 100-min timeout, unattached

## Expected impact
Users stop paying for and racing against an invisible run after closing its terminal. Risk: an accidental close now aborts real work, so a confirm may be wanted.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - closing a running terminal reaps its process
Before: 0 DELETE requests when a running session is closed (traced through the code path)
After: 1 DELETE before removal
Method: simulation - traced the close path; the render-test instrument was not built this round because abort-vs-confirm is a UX choice
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: InlineTerminal render test: running session + Close click -> assert apiFetch DELETE of the executionId (red today) and the session removed

title: A pof-cli-prompt dispatched to a busy terminal is dropped without a trace
body:
## Summary
CompactTerminal's pof-cli-prompt handler returns silently when the terminal is streaming, and dispatchPromptWhenReady is fire-and-forget, so a module action pressed during a run loses its prompt with no log, toast or retry.

## Description
src/components/cli/CompactTerminal.tsx:110 `if (... || queue.isStreaming) return;` and submitPrompt's dispatchingRef guard both drop the prompt. The senders (src/lib/cli-dispatch.ts:22, src/components/modules/ModuleShell/index.tsx:69, src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:82) receive no acknowledgement. Fixed = the terminal queues it or writes a system line 'Busy - prompt not sent', and the sender can tell (ack event).

## Flow
- start a long run in a module's terminal
- press another quick action targeting the same session
- event reaches the handler, isStreaming true -> return
- nothing in the transcript; the action appears to have done nothing

## Expected impact
Users learn their second action was not sent instead of waiting for a run that never starts. An ack touches src/lib/cli-dispatch.ts (another context).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a dropped dispatch is visible
Before: 0 log lines / 0 acks for a prompt dispatched while streaming
After: 1 system line (and an ack event the sender can read)
Method: simulation - walked the handler; instrument is a CompactTerminal test firing pof-cli-prompt while streaming
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: CompactTerminal test: pof-cli-prompt while isStreaming -> assert a 'not sent' system line (red today)

title: Terminal header shows 'Ready' after a failed, aborted or server-failed run
body:
## Summary
TerminalHeader shows Error only for lastResult.isError; a run that ended via START_FAILED or an error frame (phase 'error') or a server-arbitrated failure (STUCK_RESOLVED -> idle) renders 'Ready', because useTaskQueue's `error` has no consumer.

## Description
src/components/cli/TerminalHeader.tsx:108-116 derives the status chip from isStreaming and lastResult only. useTaskQueue returns `error` but CompactTerminal never passes it (git grep tq.error -> 0). STUCK_RESOLVED maps any outcome to phase idle, discarding success=false. Since 9bea7381 the transcript shows a failed start, but the role=status live region still announces Ready. Fixed = the header takes the error/outcome and shows Error (and Unknown for an outcomeUnknown end).

## Flow
- POST /api/claude-terminal/query fails
- reducer -> phase error, lastResult null
- header chip -> 'Ready' (announced via aria-live)

## Expected impact
Screen-reader and sighted users get a truthful run status. Low risk: header plus one prop.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the status chip reflects how the run ended
Before: 3 end paths (start failure, error frame, server-arbitrated failure) render 'Ready'
After: 0 render 'Ready'
Method: simulation - traced the three paths through reducer + header; instrument is a CompactTerminal render test per path
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: CompactTerminal render test: drive START_FAILED / error SSE / failed consult and assert the status chip reads Error, not Ready

title: InlineTerminal header buttons lack the focus ring; the resize handle is mouse-only
body:
## Summary
The Minimize and Close buttons in InlineTerminal have no focus-ring class (the other cli buttons do) and the height resize handle is a div with onMouseDown only, so keyboard users cannot see focus there nor resize the terminal.

## Description
src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:146-161 two buttons without `focus-ring` (repo token; compare src/components/cli/TerminalHeader.tsx:91,96); src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:118 resize div has no role=separator, tabIndex, aria-valuenow or key handler. Fixed = focus-ring on both buttons; a separator role with ArrowUp/ArrowDown resizing within min/max.

## Flow
- Tab through the inline terminal header
- focus lands on Minimize/Close with no visible ring
- the resize handle is never reachable by keyboard

## Expected impact
Keyboard users get visible focus and a resizable terminal. Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard parity for the inline terminal chrome
Before: focus-ring on 0/2 header buttons; resize reachable by keyboard: no
After: 2/2; yes
Method: probe - grep of focus-ring in the file returned 0; instrument is a render test asserting the classes and a keyboard-operable separator
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:146-161 (no focus-ring)
src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx:118 (onMouseDown only)
$ git grep -c focus-ring src/components/cli/InlineTerminal.tsx -> 0
instrument: InlineTerminal render test: both header buttons carry focus-ring; a role=separator handle changes inlineTerminalHeight on ArrowUp/Down

title: AntiPatternWarning debounce is a bare 600 ms literal outside UI_TIMEOUTS
body:
## Summary
The anti-pattern check debounce is hardcoded (600 ms) in the component, against the repo rule that timing values come from UI_TIMEOUTS.

## Description
src/components/cli/AntiPatternWarning.tsx:67 `}, 600);` (comment at :46). CLAUDE.md 'Timing Constants: all timing values come from UI_TIMEOUTS'. Fixed = a named UI_TIMEOUTS entry in src/lib/constants.ts (shared file, coupled) referenced here.

## Flow
- read the AntiPatternWarning debounce
- literal 600 instead of a named constant

## Expected impact
Timing becomes tunable in one place; no behaviour change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - timing literals in the shell routed through UI_TIMEOUTS
Before: 1 bare timing literal in AntiPatternWarning.tsx
After: 0
Method: probe - grep of the literal; instrument is a comment-stripped source-scan test for numeric setTimeout delays in src/components/cli
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source-scan test (comments stripped) asserting no numeric-literal setTimeout delay in src/components/cli/*.tsx; touches shared src/lib/constants.ts
